frontier.hypothesis: Target's loop-2 preheader copy is left behind by local-alloc's optimize_reg_copy_2 - the ONE remaining GCC 2.7.2 routine that can leave a physically redundant reg-reg copy in the stream, because nothing after local-alloc runs dead-code elimination. This is now the only surviving candidate: this session proved every PRE-combine copy whose destination is used only at the base add is deleted by combine, every hoisted one is deleted too, and every copy whose destination is used out-of-block leaves that use visible in the asm (our loop 1 pays for it with `move $4,$7`) where target has no such instruction.
frontier.mechanism: optimize_reg_copy_2 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/local-alloc.c:874, dispatched at local-alloc.c:1015) fires on `(set (reg D) (reg S))` where S DIES in the copy. It scans forward in the same basic block, stopping at any CODE_LABEL, JUMP_INSN, NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG or NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END, looking for a REVERSE copy `(set (reg S) (reg D))` with D dying there. If it finds one it replaces D with S over the whole range and removes both death notes - and it deletes NEITHER copy insn. Because local-alloc is the last pass that could remove them, both survive to the assembler. Note the scan-stop set: the reverse copy must sit in the preheader itself, before the loop's NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG.
frontier.next_probe: Write C that puts a reverse copy pair into loop 2's preheader, ahead of the loop: e.g. `q2 = *(u8 **)(ctx + 0xC); b2 = q2; q2 = b2; base = (u8 *)(sh2 + (s32)q2);` and variants where the round trip is spelled through the existing locals rather than new ones (`p`/`q`/`lnk` are all available and all already carry live values). Score each with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s15/score.sh, then dump the survivors with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s15/idump.sh and check F_lreg.txt for whether optimize_reg_copy_2 fired (its signature is that BOTH copies are still present and both death notes are gone). Do NOT re-probe the reuse-p family (all 8, mechanism in H-s15-5), hoisted-invariant copies whose consumer is hoisted with them (D1, 3), or anything already in the 105-entry rejected bank.

frontier.hypothesis: The hoisted-invariant lever discovered this session (H-s15-3, C1 = 6) is the right MECHANISM aimed at the wrong VALUE. C1 hoists a copy of the BASE, which lands one slot after the base add. Hoisting a copy of the ADDEND whose only use stays inside the loop body would land BEFORE the base add and be re-pointed into it by optimize_reg_copy_1 - exactly target's shape.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c's move_movables duplicates each invariant before loop_start in the order it finds them, so an invariant copy of the addend written earlier in the body than the base's uses will be emitted earlier in the preheader. If the copy's destination is then the addend that the base add consumes, optimize_reg_copy_1's precondition (SRC alive at the copy, dying at the base add, same block) is met and it rewrites the base add onto the copy's register - the two mechanisms this session named, composed. The open question is what the loop BODY can legitimately use the addend copy for, since target's loop-2 body touches only base, the links pointer and the counter.

Score with score.sh, then dump the best and check in F_loop.txt whether the copy was hoisted and in F_lreg.txt whether optimize_reg_copy_1 re-pointed the base add. Cell C1 (rejected/s15_body_invariant_copy_of_base_hoisted_copy_survives_costs_6.c) is the working reference for the emitted shape.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual is decided by local-alloc's allocno ordering, which is driven by reg_n_refs - the raw reference COUNT of the ctx+0xC pointer pseudo - and that count can be moved from C without changing any statement's meaning, by varying how many times ctx+0xC is read in the TAIL (which target itself reads three separate times). [carried unchanged from the s14 ledger; still untried, and this session gives it a sharper edge: optimize_reg_copy_1 and optimize_reg_copy_2 both ADJUST reg_n_refs by loop_depth as they rewrite, so the tail's read count feeds the very routines now named.]
frontier.mechanism: The three residual instructions are a straight SWAP of `lw a0,12(s2)` and `move a3,a0` between loop 1's exit tail and loop 2's preheader, i.e. a tie broken the other way, not a missing computation. local-alloc orders allocnos by a priority computed from reg_n_refs and live length, and optimize_reg_copy_1 (local-alloc.c:770-790) explicitly does `reg_n_refs[sregno] -= loop_depth; reg_n_refs[dregno] += loop_depth;` for every mention it rewrites - so the tail's read count is an input to the same ordering.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep the tail's ctx+0xC read count on the V1 chassis with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s15/score.sh: target reads it three times (math_Distance3D's two arguments share one read, then rec_a, then rec_b). Cells: (a) one fresh read per math_Distance3D argument (4 reads total); (b) rec_a and rec_b sharing one read (2 reads); (c) each of the four sites reading freshly; (d) the same sweep on the ctx+0x10 links pointer. Each cell is a pure duplicate-read respelling in the sanctioned family - no dead locals, no unused declarations (see rejected/unused_local_decl_q_contaminates_sweeps.c for why an unused decl invalidates a sweep). Confirm any movement in F_lreg.txt's allocno dump before believing it.
